Calculate PSD and POC flux for the 2021 and 2023 data
This uses the _PAR_Aggregated files from Ecopart.

The POC calculation scripts here copy the Matlab functions in the file processPocFluxFromUvp.m associated with the Rufas et al. (2025) GRL paper. Some lines and functions were recoded to follow R conventions.
https://github.com/annarufas/Rufas_etal_2024_GRL/blob/master/code/processPocFluxFromUvp.m

The methods explained in Rufas et al. 2025 adapting the Bisson et al. 2022 approach of the truncated power law. In the truncated power law model in Bisson et al. (2022), the modelled particle count is lower for larger particles (stronger decrease with higher lambda). 

Note that seasonal variation in POC flux is expected based on the results in the Rufas et al. 2025 aggregation (i.e., decrease in flux post-bloom).


Additionally, a MC Error propagation can be applied to account for the uncertainty in the sampling volume simular to Rufas et al. 2025.

Note that for UVP5, in Barth and Stone (2022), they removed the bottom 50m of each profile because they observed that the slowing of the CTD-rosette leads to high potential reimaging of particles.

# Functions for calculating and modeling the POC flux at each depth
The PSD is based on the LPM (large particulate material) concentrations (# L-1) by size classes.
- In the calculatePocFlux function: the psd and binMiddle inputs are arrays for each depth bin. The zeros are not removed since these are summed.
- In the calculateModelledPsd: observedVol is a single value, and observedN/binWidth/binMiddle are arrays

alpha: particle dominance (smaller value, larger particles dominate)
lambda: the particle size (mm) where power law is truncated
```{r}
calculatePOCFlux <- function(psd, binMiddle, binWidth) {
  particleEsd <- binMiddle

  # A = 2.8, b = 2.24 (used in Bisson et al. 2022)
  fluxFactor <- function(d) 2.8 * d^2.24

  pocFlux <- sum((psd/binWidth) * fluxFactor(particleEsd)*binWidth, na.rm = TRUE)

  return(pocFlux)
}


# This is Rufas et al. (2025) version of the function which was based on 
# Function modified from Rufas_etal_2024_GRL/code/processPocFluxFromUVP.m
# The value returned has units of:  mg C m-2 d-1
calculatePOCFlux_Rufas <- function(psd, binMiddle, UVP6_sizebins_width) {
  # Input:
  #   psd, # part L-1
  #   binMiddle, mm
  # 
  # Output:
  #   pocFlux, mg C m-2 d-1
  
  particleRadius <- (binMiddle / ((4/3) * pi))^(1/3)
  particleEsd <- particleRadius * 2
  
  # particleEsd <- binMiddle

  # Flux factor function from Eq. 5 in Bisson et al. (2022)
  # The parameter values are based on the Cael et al. (2021) size-sinking speed scaling relationship.
  fluxFactor <- function(d) 2.8 * d^2.24

  
  pocFlux <- sum(psd * fluxFactor(particleEsd), na.rm = TRUE)

  return(pocFlux)
}

# For the truncated power law method in Bisson et al. (2022)
# NOTE observedN is the concentration * volume sampled
calculateModelledPsd <- function(observedN, observedVol, binWidth, binMiddle) {
  # Modelled particle number (# part./um), Eq. 1 in Bisson et al. (2022)
  modelledN <- function(x, d) {
    x[1] * d^-x[2] * exp(-d / x[3])
  }
  
  # log10 transform observedN and divide by bin width
  observedN_log10 <- log10(observedN / binWidth)
  observedN_log10 <- unlist(observedN_log10)
  
  # Only consider populated size classes and remove the ones that are not
  bad <- which(is.infinite(observedN_log10))
  observedN_log10_good <- observedN_log10[-bad]
  binMiddle_good <- binMiddle[-bad]
  
  # Initial guess and bounds for model parameters
  # PP: Originally, x0 is c(40, 4, 0.1) but I changed it to c(10, 4, 0.1) to reduce the warning "Error at i = ___ :  L-BFGS-B needs finite values of 'fn'"
  #       C1    alpha lambda
  x0 <- c(10, 4, 0.1) # part L-1 / unitless / mm
  lower <- c(-Inf, 0, min(binMiddle_good))
  upper <- c(Inf, 6, max(binMiddle_good))
  
  # PP: In the original code, this is the fminsearchbnd() Matlab function.
  # Optimise model parameters using optim with box constraints (L-BFGS-B)
  opt <- stats::optim(
    par = x0,
    fn = function(x) {
      sum((observedN_log10_good - log10(modelledN(x, binMiddle_good)))^2)
    },
    method = "L-BFGS-B", 
    lower = lower,
    upper = upper
  )
  
  C1 <- opt$par[1]
  alpha <- opt$par[2]
  lambda <- opt$par[3]
  
  estimNbl <- (modelledN(opt$par, binMiddle) / observedVol) * binWidth
  
  # Remove particle size classes that are not in the observed set
  estimNbl[bad] <- NA
  
  list(estimNbl = estimNbl, C1 = C1, alpha = alpha, lambda = lambda)
}

# This approach also follows Bisson et al. (2022) but based on Rufas et al. (2025) codes
generateRandomSamplesOfParticleNumber <- function(observedNbl, observedVol, 
                                                  nIterations, N_sizebins) {
  # Assume observedNbl follows a negative binomial distribution and draw nIterations  samples from it to obtain simulatedN
  
  simulatedN <- matrix(NA, nrow = nIterations, ncol = N_sizebins)
  simulatedNbl <- matrix(NA, nrow = nIterations, ncol = N_sizebins)
  
  for (iSc in 1:N_sizebins) {
    if (observedNbl[iSc] > 0) {
      size_param <- as.numeric(observedNbl[iSc] + 1/2)
      prob_param <- 1 / (observedVol + 1)
      simulatedN[, iSc] <- rnbinom(nIterations, 
                                   size = size_param, 
                                   prob = prob_param)
      simulatedNbl[, iSc] <- simulatedN[, iSc] / observedVol
    }
  }
  
  return(simulatedNbl)
}
```

## Establish the size class bins and bin width
```{r}
# For the 15 size bin reduced dataset
bins <- uvp6_par_cnames %>% 
  filter(grepl("concentration", AnnotatedColumnName)) %>% 
  filter(Lower_limit_um >= 128 & Lower_limit_um <= 16400) %>% # to match the 0.14-16.88 mm size range in Bisson et al. (2022)
  
  # calculate the midpoint as the geometric mean instead
  mutate(Size_class_midpoint_mm = sqrt(Lower_limit_um * Upper_limit_um)/1000)
  

colStart <- which(uvp6_par_cnames$Lower_limit_um == 128)[1]-17
colEnd <- which(uvp6_par_cnames$Lower_limit_um == 16400)[1]-17

# number of bins
UVP6_N_sizebins <- nrow(bins)
# Convert um to mm
UVP6_sizebins_edges_mm <- c(bins$Lower_limit_um) / 1000
# Get width of size bins
UVP6_sizebins_width <- bins$Size_class_width_mm
# Get midpoints of size bins
UVP6_sizebins_mid <- bins$Size_class_midpoint_mm

```



## POC Flux Calculations
```{r}
nIterations <- 100

pocFlux_UVP6 <- uvp6_PAR %>% 
  select(sample_id, project,
         date, time, Depth_5m, Sampled_volume_L) %>% 
  mutate(ObsFlux = NA, ModelFlux = NA, 
         fluxIter = NA, fluxIterSD = NA, fluxIterN = NA,
         C1 = NA, alpha = NA, lambda = NA)

# This loop copies the script in Section 3 of processPocFluxFromUvp.m (Rufas et al. 2025). 
for (i in c(1:nrow(pocFlux_UVP6))) {
  a_par <- uvp6_PAR[i, colStart:colEnd]
  a_vol <- uvp6_PAR$Sampled_volume_L[i]
  
  # No truncated power law model
  pocFlux_UVP6$ObsFlux[i] <- calculatePOCFlux(a_par, UVP6_sizebins_mid, 
                                              UVP6_sizebins_width)
  
  # With truncated power law model
  observedN <- round( a_par * a_vol )
  if(sum(observedN) > 0){
    tryCatch( {
      trunc <- calculateModelledPsd(observedN, a_vol, 
                                    UVP6_sizebins_width, UVP6_sizebins_mid )
      
      pocFlux_UVP6$ModelFlux[i] <- calculatePOCFlux(trunc$estimNbl,
                                                    UVP6_sizebins_mid,
                                                    UVP6_sizebins_width)
      pocFlux_UVP6$C1[i] <- trunc$C1
      pocFlux_UVP6$alpha[i] <- trunc$alpha
      pocFlux_UVP6$lambda[i] <- trunc$lambda
    },
    error = function(e){cat("ERROR: at i =", i, " ", 
                            conditionMessage(e), "\n")})
    
    
    # Add the random samples function for sample volume error
    simulatedNbl <- generateRandomSamplesOfParticleNumber(
      a_par, a_vol, nIterations, 
      N_sizebins = UVP6_N_sizebins)
    
    fluxIter <- rep(NA, nIterations)
    for (iIter in seq_len(nIterations)) {
      if (sum(simulatedNbl[iIter, ], na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
        fluxIter[iIter] <- calculatePOCFlux(simulatedNbl[iIter, ],
                                            UVP6_sizebins_mid,UVP6_sizebins_width)
      }
    }
    pocFlux_UVP6$fluxIterSD[i] <- sd(fluxIter, na.rm = TRUE)
    # Add average iterated flux and the sample size
    pocFlux_UVP6$fluxIter[i] <- mean(fluxIter, na.rm = TRUE)
    pocFlux_UVP6$fluxIterN[i] <- length(!is.na(fluxIter))
  } 
}

pocFluxErr_UVP6 <- pocFlux_UVP6 %>%
  filter(is.na(ModelFlux))

# temporary save of results
save(pocFlux_UVP6, bins,
file = "data/POC_flux_UVP6_confident_20260326.RData")
```

# ------------------------
# ******** UVP5 ********

Data processing and POC flux analysis 
As an additional source of POC flux estimates, the compiled UVP5 data from Kiko et al. (2022) is used and similarly analyzed. The seasonal variation could be estimated since the historical sampling spans from April to October. 

Tasks: 
1. curate the samples further
2. assign regions to each sample
3. reorganize the script to match the UVP6 calculations


## Load and prep data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
`%notin%` <- Negate(`%in%`)

load("data/uvp6_images_calculated_traits_20260321.RData")
rm(indiv_traits, volumes.df)

# Load data
load('C:/Sync/UVP5_Data_Kikoetal2022/Canadian_Arctic_subset.RData')

# Find nearest neighbor to UVP6 sample locations and use that as basis for the region assignment
# Convert to sf points
UVP5_sf <- UVP5_CA_Arctic_meta %>% 
  # minimum depth
  filter(Deepest_Bin >= 200) %>% 
  distinct(Profile, Cruise, Date_Time, Latitude, Longitude) %>% 
  st_as_sf(coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

UVP6_sf <- Amund_UVP6_meta %>% 
  select(sample_stationid_ed, region.inuktitut,
         Longitude = object_lon, Latitude = object_lat) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

# Find nearest UVP6 point for each UVP5 point
nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(UVP5_sf, UVP6_sf)

# Assign region from nearest UVP6 station
UVP5_region <- UVP5_sf %>%
  mutate(
    nearest_stationid_ed = UVP6_sf$sample_stationid_ed[nearest_idx],
    region.inuktitut = UVP6_sf$region.inuktitut[nearest_idx],
    dist_m = st_distance(geometry, UVP6_sf$geometry[nearest_idx], 
                         by_element = TRUE) %>% 
      as.numeric()
  ) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  # convert the Qikiqtaluup Ikinga (Davis Strait) below 65N to Nunatsiavut
  mutate(region.inuktitut = 
           if_else(Latitude < 65 & 
                     region.inuktitut == "Qikiqtaaluup Ikinga\n(Davis Strait)",
         "Nunatsiavut Shelf\n(Labrador Shelf)", region.inuktitut)) %>% 
  mutate(region.inuktitut = factor(region.inuktitut,
                                   levels = levels(region_rename$region.inuktitut)))
  # remove some points in the fjords?

rm(UVP5_sf, UVP6_sf, nearest_idx)
```

## Curate the UVP5 profiles and establish size bins
```{r}
UVP5_CA_Arctic <- UVP5_CA_Arctic %>% 
  filter(Profile %in% UVP5_region$Profile) %>% 
  select(Profile, 
         Depth_5m = Pressure_dbar, Volume_L,
         concentration_128_161:concentration_16_20) 

UVP5_CA_Arctic_meta <- UVP5_CA_Arctic_meta %>% 
  filter(Profile %in% UVP5_region$Profile)


UVP5_sizebins_edges_mm <- c(0.128,0.161,0.203,0.256,0.323,0.406,0.512,0.645,0.813,1.02,1.29,1.63,2.05,2.58,3.25,4.1,5.16,6.5,8.19,10.3,13,16.4,20.6) 

UVP5_bins <- data.frame(Lower_limit_mm = UVP5_sizebins_edges_mm[1:22],
                   Upper_limit_mm = UVP5_sizebins_edges_mm[2:23]) %>% 
  # calculate bin width
  mutate(UVP6_sizebins_width = Upper_limit_mm - Lower_limit_mm) %>% 
  # calculate the midpoint as the geometric mean instead
  mutate(Size_class_midpoint_mm = sqrt(Lower_limit_mm * Upper_limit_mm))
  
UVP5_N_sizebins <- nrow(UVP5_bins)
# Get width of size bins
UVP5_sizebins_width <- UVP5_bins$UVP6_sizebins_width
# Get midpoints of size bins
UVP5_sizebins_mid <- UVP5_bins$Size_class_midpoint_mm
```

## POC Flux calculation
Only run if there are new calculations, else load the output file.
```{r, eval=FALSE}
pocFlux_UVP5 <- UVP5_CA_Arctic %>% 
  select(Profile,
         Depth_5m, Volume_L) %>% 
  mutate(ObsFlux = NA, ModelFlux = NA, C1 = NA, alpha = NA, lambda = NA)

for (i in c(1:nrow(pocFlux_UVP5))) {
  a_par <- UVP5_CA_Arctic[i, 4:25]
  a_vol <- UVP5_CA_Arctic$Volume_L[i]
  
   # No model
  pocFlux_UVP5$ObsFlux[i] <- calculatePOCFlux(a_par, UVP5_sizebins_mid,
                                              UVP5_sizebins_width)
  
  # With truncated power law model
  observedN <- round( a_par * a_vol )
  if(sum(observedN) > 0){
    tryCatch( {
      trunc <- calculateModelledPsd(observedN, a_vol, 
                                    UVP5_sizebins_width, UVP5_sizebins_mid )
      
      pocFlux_UVP5$ModelFlux[i] <- calculatePOCFlux(trunc$estimNbl,
                                                    UVP5_sizebins_mid,
                                                    UVP5_sizebins_width)
      pocFlux_UVP5$C1[i] <- trunc$C1
      pocFlux_UVP5$alpha[i] <- trunc$alpha
      pocFlux_UVP5$lambda[i] <- trunc$lambda
    },
    error = function(e){cat("ERROR: at i =", i, " ", 
                            conditionMessage(e), "\n")})
  }
}

# Export results to limit recalculations of this long loop
save(file = "data/UVP5_CA_Arctic_POCFLUX_results_20260326.RData",
     pocFlux_UVP5, UVP5_CA_Arctic, UVP5_CA_Arctic_meta, UVP5_region)
```

Calculate regional integrated annual flux
```{r}
pocFlux_region_annual <- pocFlux_UVP5_profiles %>%   
   # consider only stations with at least 250m depth?
  filter(Depth_5m >= 150 & Depth_5m < 250) %>% 
  
  # average the flux for the 200 m layer
  group_by(Profile, region.inuktitut) %>%
  summarise(ModelFlux = mean(ModelFlux),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  # average values per region and month
  group_by(region.inuktitut) %>%
  summarise(ModelFlux_mean = mean(ModelFlux),
            ModelFlux_sd = sd(ModelFlux),
            nprofiles = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  mutate(poc_model_184 = (ModelFlux_mean * 184 / 1000), 
         poc_model_365 = (ModelFlux_mean * 184 / 1000) + 
           (ModelFlux_mean/4 * 181 / 1000)) 

ggplot(pocFlux_region_annual %>% 
         filter(region.inuktitut != "Nares Strait"), aes(x = region.inuktitut,
                                                         y = poc_model_365)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") 
```


# *** test poc flux equations
```{r}
calculatePOCFluxES <- function(psd, binMiddle, binWidth) {
  # A = 2.8, b = 2.24
  fluxFactor <- function(d) 2.8 * d^2.24

  pocFluxA <- sum((psd/binWidth) * fluxFactor(binMiddle)*binWidth, na.rm = TRUE)
  pocFluxB <- sum(psd * fluxFactor(binMiddle), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Rufas et al
  particleRadius <- (binMiddle / ((4/3) * pi))^(1/3)
  particleEsd <- particleRadius * 2
  pocFluxC <- sum((psd/binWidth) * fluxFactor(particleEsd)*binWidth, na.rm = TRUE)
  pocFluxD <- sum(psd * fluxFactor(particleEsd), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  df <- data.frame(pocFluxA, pocFluxB, pocFluxC, pocFluxD)
  return(df)
}

pocFlux_UVP6_test <- uvp6_PAR %>% 
  select(sample_id, project,
         date, time, Depth_5m, Sampled_volume_L) %>% 
  mutate(pocFluxA = NA, pocFluxB = NA, pocFluxC = NA, pocFluxD = NA)

# This loop copies the script in Section 3 of processPocFluxFromUvp.m (Rufas et al. 2025). 
for (i in c(1:5000)) {
  a_par <- uvp6_PAR[i, colStart:colEnd]
  a_vol <- uvp6_PAR$Sampled_volume_L[i]
  
  flux_results <- calculatePOCFluxES(a_par, UVP6_sizebins_mid, 
                                              UVP6_sizebins_width)
  
  pocFlux_UVP6_test$pocFluxA[i] <- flux_results$pocFluxA
  pocFlux_UVP6_test$pocFluxB[i] <- flux_results$pocFluxB
  pocFlux_UVP6_test$pocFluxC[i] <- flux_results$pocFluxC
  pocFlux_UVP6_test$pocFluxD[i] <- flux_results$pocFluxD
}
```
